newsitem.title: USA: L.A. to sue over California tax measure - report.
newsitem.headline: L.A. to sue over California tax measure - report.

text.p: The Los Angeles City Council has decided to sue over a California measure that will constrain the ability of local governments to impose fees, assessments and taxes, the Los Angeles Times reported on Saturday.

Proposition 218, which was approved by California voters on November 5, had drawn fire from local government officials and municipal analysts. Los Angeles could be the first local government to go to court over the measure.

In the debate that preceded the 8-to-3 vote which directed the city attorney to prepare a lawsuit, council members zeroed in on a provision of the measure that allows only property owners a vote on most types of assessments, the Times reported.

Proposition 218 would strengthen existing law to require that new local taxes be submitted to voters for approval. It would also allow property owners to approve new assessments and strictly limit the use of fees and charges.
Moody's Investors Service warned earlier this week that the credit ratings of some local governments in the state could be undermined by a controversial tax measure.
